observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: Binary white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410/eRASSU J191213.9-441044; secure Gaia DR3 counterpart 6712706405280342784. Pelisoli+23 MeerKAT L-band Fig. 1 reports peak image brightness up to about 15 mJy/beam, not integrated flux density. Schwope+23 reports epoch- and band-specific X-ray measurements; eRASS1 0.2-2.3 keV flux is 3.2 x 10^-13 in Table 1 and 3.3 +/- 0.7 x 10^-13 in the abstract; fixed 1-10 and 0.1-10 keV columns remain NA. Orbital period 0.16811989(36) d; 2022 WD spin 319.34903(8) s. See J1912 measurement ledger for observed/unabsorbed X-ray conventions and 2025 candidate results.

issues.competing_evidence: Discovery Pelisoli+23 reports M1=1.2 +/- 0.2 Msun and an inclination ceiling below 37 deg from optical/Roche assumptions, including H-beta/L1 geometry. HST/COS Pelisoli+23_J1912UV fits give adopted M1=0.59 +/- 0.05 Msun; updated UV metal-line/Roche analysis gives i=59 +/- 6 deg, and q constraints change. The UV paper says the former mass is about 3 sigma above its fit.
issues.why_it_matters: Changes component masses, binary geometry, and any population/evolutionary comparison; the two results use different tracers and model assumptions.
issues.needed_action: Choose whether the public wide table should expose the later UV atmosphere/model mass as provisional or leave a scalar blank/unresolved. Preserve both values and methods in the ledger; verify the dynamical line-tracer/Roche correction before adopting a single mass.

issues.competing_evidence: Pelisoli+23_J1912UV Table 2 prints individual radii 0.0131, 0.0119, 0.0138 Rsun (each +/-0.004) but the adopted row prints 0.128 +/- 0.040 Rsun. The accepted manuscript PDF table was visually checked; the discrepancy is present in the printed table.
issues.why_it_matters: The adopted value is physically inconsistent with the individual fits/mass scale by about a factor of ten; blindly correcting it would invent an unpublished correction.
issues.needed_action: Ask authors or check a publisher correction/version of record for the adopted radius and the printed radius uncertainties. Keep all literal table values and leave the preferred radius unset until verified.

issues.competing_evidence: Discovery optical timing gives 319.34903(8) s. Meintjes+25 reports 270.504287(20) cycles/day; direct conversion gives 319.4034407 s, while Fig. 2 prints 5.323392264(40) min (319.4035358 s) and the abstract/§3.2 narrative print 5.32339264(40) min (319.4035584 s). The proceeding says O-C work is planned and no period derivative is reported.
issues.why_it_matters: A period difference could reflect timing/systematics, a period change, or transcription; treating it as a measured spin-down would affect field/torque inference.
issues.needed_action: Retain the discovery and 2025 values separately. Ask the authors to clarify the frequency-to-period/narrative transcription difference and obtain a phase-connected timing solution/O-C analysis before deriving Pdot or replacing the discovery spin.

issues.competing_evidence: Minnie+25 reports a possible 0.5-10 GeV pulse at 319.99 +/- 0.34 s using 2009-2024 LAT data. The body gives pre-trials periodogram FAP 1.74e-7 and labels it about 5.74 sigma, while standard Gaussian one/two-sided conversion is about 5.10/5.23 sigma. It gives H-test H~30, Prob(>H)=6.14e-6 (~4.37 sigma); the abstract/Fig. 1 caption pair -log(Pr)=6.76 with ~4.37 sigma, apparently mixing periodogram and H-test statistics. The phase fold uses the discovery ephemeris, but 15-year phase coherence is not demonstrated; no integrated flux is reported.
issues.why_it_matters: This could add a high-energy emission component, but accepting an unconfirmed period/phase claim would affect the source’s emission classification.
issues.needed_action: Seek an independent Fermi-LAT reanalysis or replication with event selection, trials accounting, H-test probability, phase-connected ephemeris and pulse significance documented. Ask authors to clarify the abstract/caption significance pairing; until then label it a conference-reported candidate only.

issues.competing_evidence: Discovery/X-ray/UV papers describe a WDP and discuss possible flaring/residual mass transfer; discovery estimates the donor may fill >90% of its Roche lobe, while UV geometry updates the inclination and mass constraints. The 2025 MeerKAT proceeding uses a detached-WDP framing but adds no donor-state measurement.
issues.why_it_matters: Detached versus semi-detached status and residual transfer affect mechanistic/evolutionary comparisons, but the current observations do not establish one unique state.
issues.needed_action: Keep the observed WDP classification. Before assigning a catalog detached/semi-detached flag, decide what evidence standard to use and seek phase-resolved accretion/donor diagnostics; do not infer an evolutionary sequence from the analogy with AR Sco.
